verdict.rationale: First-party docs show Codex acting as an MCP client. Users can add local (stdio) or remote MCP servers via `codex mcp add`, authenticate when needed, and inspect the available tools before use. `/mcp` lists active servers in the TUI, and the configuration is shared across the CLI, IDE extension and desktop app. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of MCP client use, and detailed docs on remote-server/auth configuration beyond the summary mention.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Add local or remote MCP servers, authenticate when needed, and inspect the tools available to the current session before Codex uses them.
codex mcp add <server-name> --env VAR1=VALUE1 --env VAR2=VALUE2 -- <stdio server-command>
In the `codex` TUI, use `/mcp` to see your active MCP servers.
Once you configure your MCP servers, you can switch among those clients without redoing setup.
